name: SQL and AI Training Data Pipelines
title: SQL and AI Training Data Pipelines
answer: SQL and AI training data pipelines cover the work of turning rows held in operational databases into datasets that training and fine tuning jobs can read. The usual shape is an extract from a source system, a set of cleaning and joining steps written in SQL, and a load into storage the training job can reach. Because the queries decide what the model sees, an error in a join or a filter becomes an error the model learns from. The topic sits at the meeting point of data engineering and machine learning practice rather than inside either one alone.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the databases an organisation already operates, most often PostgreSQL, MySQL, or a warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift, with object storage holding the finished dataset. Orchestration is commonly handled by tools like Airflow or dbt, which schedule the SQL and track what each run produced.Every page on this site is itself built from a PostgreSQL database, which is a fair illustration of how ordinary relational storage sits under AI work.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A pipeline typically starts with a snapshot or change data capture from the source, then applies SQL to deduplicate, normalise types, resolve entities, and join in labels or features. The result is written out in a columnar format such as Parquet, often split into train, validation, and test sets, with a manifest recording which query version produced which file. Practitioners check row counts, null rates, and label distributions before a run, and compare a new dataset against the previous one to see what changed. Version control for the SQL matters as much as version control for the model, since a silent change in a filter can shift the training distribution.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main concerns are provenance, consent, and the rights attached to the rows being reused. A pipeline that copies personal data into a training set inherits the obligations that applied to the source, including retention limits, deletion requests, and any contractual restriction on secondary use. Teams therefore keep lineage from each training record back to its source table and query, and record who approved the extract. Access controls on the training store, masking of direct identifiers, and a documented process for removing a record from a dataset are common practice. None of this is legal advice, and the specific rules depend on jurisdiction and on the data involved.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward treating training data as a managed product with its own tests, contracts, and release notes, rather than as a one off export. More of the transformation logic is moving into versioned SQL models that can be reviewed and rerun, and AI assistants are being given read access to warehouses so that dataset questions can be answered in place. Expect tighter coupling between the query layer and the training job, with lineage captured automatically at run time. The open question is how quickly deletion and consent workflows catch up with the pace at which datasets are rebuilt.
